epithet: The uncle whom kinship could not save
lede: The Prophet ﷺ stood on the hill of Ṣafā and called his people to hear the first public warning. His own uncle answered with a curse. The curse was returned in five ayat, and the man lived another ten years without being able to prove them wrong.

names.name: al-Masad
names.note: After its last word: the twisted rope round the neck of Abū Lahab’s wife.

names.name: Tabbat
names.note: Its opening word, and the name both Ibn al-Jawzī and al-Qurṭubī head it with. It is also called Sūrat Abī Lahab.

revelation.detail: It is Makkan without disagreement, and its occasion is narrated in both Ṣaḥīḥs. The traditional order places it sixth: it came down at the very start of the open call.
revelation.when: The day the call was first made in public, from the hill of Ṣafā — about the third year of the mission

evidence.quote: وَهِيَ مَكِّيَّةٌ بِإجْماعِهِمْ وَسَبَبُ نُزُولِها ما رَوى البُخارِيُّ ومُسْلِمٌ في " الصَّحِيحَيْنِ " مِن حَدِيثِ سَعِيدِ بْنِ جُبَيْرٍ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ
سُورَةُ "تَبَّتْ" وَهِيَ مَكِّيَّةٌ بِإِجْمَاعٍ. وَهِيَ خُمْسُ آيات

attested.quote: أخْرَجَ ابْنُ مَرْدُويَهَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ قالَ: نَزَلَتْ ﴿تَبَّتْ يَدا أبِي لَهَبٍ﴾ بِمَكَّةَ
attested.says: Ibn ʿAbbās: it came down in Makkah. Recorded by Ibn Mardawayh.

setting: For the first years the Prophet ﷺ called people to Islam quietly, one household at a time. Then came the command: “And warn your nearest kindred” (26:214).

Ibn ʿAbbās tells what he did. He went out and climbed Ṣafā, the low hill beside the Kaʿbah from which a man could be heard across the town, and gave the cry the Arabs used for a dawn attack: Yā ṣabāḥāh! Quraysh gathered. He said: “Tell me — if I told you that cavalry were coming out from the foot of this mountain, would you believe me?” They said: “We have never known you to lie.” He said: “Then I am a warner to you, ahead of a severe punishment.”
Abū Lahab — ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, his father’s brother — spoke first. “May you perish for the rest of the day! Is it for this that you gathered us?” And this surah came down.

He and his wife Umm Jamīl, the sister of Abū Sufyān, were neighbours of the Prophet ﷺ and among the most persistent of those who harmed him. The surah says that he will enter a blazing fire — which is to say that he will die a disbeliever. He heard it. He had roughly a decade in which to say the words of faith, even insincerely, and call the Qurʾan a liar. He never did. He died after Badr, of a disease that kept his own sons from going near his body.

occasions.title: The call from Ṣafā
occasions.text: When “And warn your nearest kindred” came down, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ climbed Ṣafā and called out until Quraysh had gathered, and warned them. Abū Lahab said: “May you perish for the rest of this day! Was it for this that you gathered us?” So there came down: “Perish the two hands of Abū Lahab, and perish he.”

aim: That lineage and standing are of no use alongside disbelief in Allah.

outline.title: Abū Lahab
outline.summary: Perish the two hands of Abū Lahab, and perish he. His wealth has not availed him, nor what he earned. He will enter a fire of blazing flame — lahab, the very word he was nicknamed by.

outline.title: His wife
outline.summary: And his wife, the carrier of firewood: around her neck, a rope of palm fibre. She carried thorns to strew in the Prophet’s ﷺ path, and carried tales to set people against him; the early commentators give both.

keyAyah.why: The curse, turned back on the one who spoke it — the only one of the Prophet’s ﷺ enemies in Makkah to be condemned in the Qurʾan by name.

before: Al-Naṣr shows the end of the mission, with the tribes entering Islam in crowds. Al-Masad shows its first public day, and the nearest of his kin refusing.
after: A man’s lineage could not save him. Al-Ikhlāṣ turns to the One who has no lineage at all: He neither begets nor is born.

notable.label: Perish the hands of Abū Lahab
His wealth did not avail him
